Variants.Content: Edinburgh Castle dominated Lothian from its precipitous volcanic crag. Housing the Scottish royal court, records, and treasury, its craggy approaches commanded sweeping vistas of the Firth of Forth while repelling mechanical siege assaults.
Natural cliff walls and deep mountain wells made the rock fortress nearly impregnable, anchoring Alexander III's centralized crown governance.
